title: add vpc control plane terraform: multi-az subnets + interface endpoints + peering + route53
description:
Add Terraform modules and provisioning logic to create a VPC-backed private control plane for Redwood Private. This PR implements multi-AZ subnet provisioning, interface endpoints for SSM/EC2/SecretsManager, security group defaults for control plane components, cross-account VPC peering helpers, and automated Route53 private hosted zone peering and records. Motivation: customers deploying Redwood Private in VPC/on-prem networks need a repeatable, secure network topology that supports private control plane connectivity, cross-account management, and DNS visibility for private hosted zones. This PR consolidates previous ad-hoc scripts into a single reusable module and adds upgrade hooks and rollback safety checks for installer-driven upgrades.

Scope and changes (high level):
- New Terraform module: modules/vpc-control-plane
  - multi_az subnets resource (public/private convention for control-plane and worker control subnets)
  - interface_endpoints submodule to create AWS interface endpoints with target services and private DNS
  - security_groups.tf with conservative inbound/outbound defaults and explicit rules for control plane services
  - peering submodule to support cross-account peering with optional aws_ram and accepter logic
  - route53_peering helper to create private hosted zone associations and optional cross-account delegation records
- Installer integration
  - private-installer/terraform/main.tf imports modules/vpc-control-plane and wires variables from installer config
  - upgrade hooks: private-installer/upgrade/terraform-hooks.tf adds preflight checks and conditional resources to allow safe incremental upgrades
- Helm chart / values changes
  - charts/private-control-plane/values.schema.json updated to include vpc metadata for DNS/peering
- Docs: docs/private/vpc-control-plane-terraform.md (usage, examples, and upgrade notes)

Implementation notes: The module is intentionally conservative: by default it creates dedicated control-plane subnets and non-default security groups to avoid accidental exposure. Interface endpoints are optional and controlled via variables (create_ssm_endpoint, create_secrets_endpoint, etc.). Peering is opt-in and supports both same-account and cross-account flows using aws_vpc_peering_connection + route propagation where supported. Route53 association uses aws_route53_zone_association for same-account and a custom flow with delegation records + IAM-signed pre-signed changes for cross-account (documented in the module README).

Upgrade and rollback: To reduce blast radius during upgrades we add terraform-based preflight checks: validating CIDR non-overlap, required IAM roles present, and checking for existing hosted zone conflicts. The installer now runs a dry-run plan and a 'peering-check' step to confirm route tables allow control plane reachability. Rollback notes are included in docs and implemented using a set of safe defaults that avoid destructive replaces (resource lifecycle rules set to create_before_destroy where feasible).

Testing and CI: Module includes unit-style terraform tests (terratest wrappers) and an integration pipeline to spin up a minimal VPC in the CI account. Tests added: terraform fmt, validate, tflint, terratest/vpc_control_plane_integration.sh. The PR also includes an e2e smoke test that verifies control plane API endpoint resolution via the created Route53 private hosted zone.

Checklist:
- [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Installer wiring and upgrade hooks added
- [x] Helm values/schema updated
- [x] Docs and usage examples added
- [x] Terratest integration added to CI
- [x] Security review of security groups and endpoints complete

Related work: Linear ENG-4231, ENG-4298; references previous private-installer PRs for single-AZ flows (pr-430001, pr-431789). This PR is intentionally scoped to network provisioning and does not change control plane application manifests.

review_comments: Aditi Rao: Please add a note about the expected IAM roles for cross-account peering in the module README. Also suggest setting create_ssm_endpoint=false by default for smaller customers.
Maya Chen: Added IAM notes to README and flipped default for create_ssm_endpoint to false; updated tests to cover both enabled/disabled cases.
Lukas Meyer: Security group rules look good; consider adding an explicit deny for traffic from public CIDRs in case of misconfig. Optional: add a CI check to detect overly permissive CIDRs.
Maya Chen: Implemented deny rule and added a tflint rule to warn on 0.0.0.0/0 ingress for control-plane SGs. Added note in release notes.
Priya Nair: Can we ensure route53 associations are idempotent across accounts? The association flow looks ok but add a guard for existing associations to avoid plan failures.
Maya Chen: Added existence checks and a replace_with_create_before_destroy lifecycle where applicable; documented the idempotency behavior.
release_notes: Adds a reusable Terraform module to provision multi-AZ VPC networking for the private control plane: subnets, interface endpoints, security groups, peering helpers, and Route53 private hosted zone peering. Includes installer hooks for safe upgrades and CI integration tests.
